title: The Andes Survivors
text:
On 13 October 1972 a Uruguayan Air Force plane carrying the Old Christians rugby team from Montevideo, with friends and family, crashed high in the Andes on the border between Chile and Argentina. Of the 45 people aboard, many died in the crash or soon after. The survivors were stranded on a glacier, in the snow, with almost no food, little warm clothing and no means of rescue. After ten days they heard on a radio that the search had been called off.

The group organized itself to survive. Two medical students, Roberto Canessa and Gustavo Zerbino, tended the injured. Others melted snow into drinking water using aluminum sheets from the wreck, kept the fuselage sealed against the cold, and divided chores. When the food ran out, the survivors faced a terrible choice and decided, after long discussion, to eat the bodies of the dead to stay alive. Several of them agreed that if they died, the others could do the same with their bodies.

An avalanche on 29 October buried the fuselage and killed eight more. In December, after earlier attempts, Nando Parrado and Roberto Canessa set out to cross the mountains on foot toward Chile. After about ten days of climbing and walking, they met a Chilean muleteer, Sergio Catalan, who raised the alarm.

Helicopters reached the crash site on 22 and 23 December. Sixteen people survived after seventy-two days in the mountains.
lesson: In extreme crisis, groups survive by organizing: dividing tasks, deciding hard things together and trusting a few to go for help.
people: Nando Parrado, Roberto Canessa, Gustavo Zerbino, Old Christians rugby team
source: Piers Paul Read, Alive: The Story of the Andes Survivors (1974)
